ai.description: This lizard reaches 20 cm in total length. It is olive-brown with dark dorsal cross-bands and a distinct white stripe along the upper lip. A prominent nuchal crest and granular scales define it.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Japalura kumaonensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous row of enlarged, spine-like scales along the nape and mid-dorsal region.
ai.habitat: The Kumaon Mountain Lizard inhabits temperate forests and rocky areas in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kumaon mountain lizard is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects and invertebrates on tree trunks and rocky surfaces during the warmer daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Japalura kumaonensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 4–8 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Japalura kumaonensis* is endemic to the Western Himalayas, primarily occurring in the Indian states of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh at elevations of 1,500–3,000 meters.
